title: Modular Building Block Construction
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D modular building block construction system using Three.js (CDN). The scene allows users to place, stack, rotate, and delete colored building blocks on a grid-based foundation to construct architectural structures.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (12, 10, 12) looking at the origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Add a directional light at (5, 15, 5) with intensity 1.0 and an ambient light with intensity 0.4.
- Create a ground plane: 20x20 unit flat grid (GridHelper with divisions=20 over a PlaneGeometry), colored #8B8B8B.
- Enable shadows on the renderer and directional light. The ground plane receives shadows.

## Block System
- Blocks are BoxGeometry units of size 1x1x1.
- Available block colors (cycle with 'C' key): red (#e74c3c), blue (#3498db), green (#2ecc71), yellow (#f1c40f), purple (#9b59b6). Default is red (index 0).
- A translucent ghost block (opacity 0.4) follows the mouse cursor on the grid, snapping to integer grid positions. The ghost block shows where the next block will be placed.
- Ghost block must snap to the nearest integer X and Z, and Y must be the lowest available Y at that (X,Z) column (auto-stacking). Y of the first block on ground is 0.5 (half-height above ground).

## Interactions
- LEFT CLICK on the grid/ghost position: Place a solid block at the ghost block's snapped position. Each placed block is added to an internal block list.
- RIGHT CLICK on an existing block: Delete that block. Blocks above it should drop down (gravity collapse) so no floating blocks remain.
- 'C' key: Cycle the active color to the next in the palette.
- 'R' key: Rotate the ghost block 90 degrees around Y axis (track rotation as 0, 90, 180, 270 degrees). Even though blocks are cubes, track and apply rotation for visual consistency.
- 'U' key: Undo the last placement (remove the most recently placed block). Only undoes placements, not deletions.
- 'G' key: Toggle gravity mode. When gravity is ON (default), blocks auto-stack. When OFF, blocks can be placed at any Y level (ghost block Y follows a vertical offset controlled by mouse wheel: scroll up = +1Y, scroll down = -1Y, clamped 0.5 to 10.5).
- Arrow Up / Arrow Down: Move the camera target Y position up/down by 1 unit (to inspect tall structures). Clamp between 0 and 15.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left HUD panel (HTML overlay, id='hud-panel') showing:
  - 'Blocks Placed: N' (span id='block-count')
  - 'Active Color: <colorName>' (span id='active-color')
  - 'Rotation: <degrees>°' (span id='rotation-display')
  - 'Gravity: ON/OFF' (span id='gravity-status')
  - 'Max Height: N' (span id='max-height') — tallest column in blocks
  - 'Camera Target Y: N' (span id='camera-target-y')

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields, updated every frame or on interaction:
- blockCount: number of placed blocks (integer)
- activeColorIndex: current color palette index (0-4)
- activeColorName: string name of current color ('red','blue','green','yellow','purple')
- rotation: ghost block Y rotation in degrees (0, 90, 180, 270)
- gravityEnabled: boolean
- maxHeight: integer, tallest stack height in blocks (0 if no blocks)
- ghostPosition: {x, y, z} of the ghost block center
- blocks: array of objects {x, y, z, color, id} for each placed block
- cameraTargetY: number, current orbit target Y
- lastAction: string describing last action ('place', 'delete', 'undo', 'colorChange', 'rotate', 'gravityToggle', 'none')
- floatingBlocks: number of blocks with empty space below them (should be 0 when gravity is on)
- totalVolume: number equal to blockCount (each block is 1 cubic unit)
- undoStackSize: number of blocks available to undo

## Physics / Constraints
- When gravity is ON, no block may float: every block at Y=0.5 is grounded, every block at Y>0.5 must have a block directly below it at Y-1.
- Deleting a block triggers a gravity collapse: all blocks above in the same (X,Z) column shift down to fill the gap.
- Block positions must always be at integer X, Z and half-integer Y (0.5, 1.5, 2.5, ...).
- No two blocks may occupy the same (X, Z, Y) position.
- All numerical state values must be finite (no NaN, no Infinity).
physics_constraints: Gravity stacking: blocks auto-stack with no floating blocks when gravity is enabled. Deleting a block causes all blocks above in the same column to collapse downward. Block positions snap to integer grid (X,Z) and half-integer Y. No overlapping blocks allowed. Conservation: totalVolume must always equal blockCount.
